purpose: Standalone, uncalibrated development simulation of a one-STS vehicle-readiness policy. It is not a terminal model or a native CHESSCON run.

controller.selection: lowest ETA eligible vehicle; one physical staged vehicle; reactive fallback when staging cannot be reserved
controller.forecast: At move start, R1 uses a nominal 130 s STS-service forecast and reevaluates at 5 s ticks. It commits the physical stage reservation only at the final grid tick 10 to <15 s before that forecast. It does not observe the realised future STS service draw or a potential post-selection vehicle-delay event.

congestion.description: Synthetic congestion condition: each transport/yard triangular mean is multiplied by 1.25 and each deviation from that original triangular mean is multiplied by 1.5.

disruption.description: Synthetic congestion plus task blocks and vehicle-delay events.

randomness.method: SHA-256-derived independent random streams keyed by condition, seed, task, vehicle, and event label. R0 and R1 consume the same exogenous tape for a condition and seed. Vehicle-delay draws materialise after vehicle selection and are not exposed to either policy's ETA rank.

metrics.primary: mean inter-cycle dwell over moves 2-120: sum(start of STS service_i - completion of STS service_(i-1)) / 119

analysis.paired_difference_convention: For dwell, improvement is R0 minus R1 so positive values indicate less R1 dwell. For throughput, delta is R1 minus R0 so positive values indicate higher R1 throughput.

timing_semantics.direct_reactive_handoff: Reactive post-demand vehicle-presentation delay. It is the same presentation primitive R1 may complete before the demand point.
timing_semantics.staged_handoff: Common final physical handoff/attachment primitive used by both R0 and R1 after a vehicle is present. It is not an R1-only faster transfer input.
